Back: Nonempty set \(V\) with \(+\) and scalar mult satisfying 10 axioms: closure under \(+\) and scalar mult; associativity and commutativity of \(+\); additive identity \(\mathbf{0}\); additive inverse; two distributive laws; associativity of scalar mult; scalar identity 1.
H is a subspace of V iff: (1) \(\mathbf{0} \in H\); (2) \(\mathbf{u},\mathbf{v} \in H \implies \mathbf{u}+\mathbf{v} \in H\); (3) \(\mathbf{u} \in H \implies c\mathbf{u} \in H\). All three required.
\(\text{Span}\{\mathbf{v}_1,\ldots,\mathbf{v}_k\}\) is always a subspace. Use to skip the 10 axioms ONLY IF \(H\) is already expressed as an explicit span.
\(\text{Null}(A) = \{\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^n : A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{0}\}\). Basis: solve \(A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}\); write parametric solution; extract free-variable vectors.

\(\text{Col}(A)\) = Span of columns of \(A\) = range of \(\mathbf{x} \mapsto A\mathbf{x}\). Basis: pivot columns of ORIGINAL \(A\). Warning: RREF changes column vectors — do NOT use pivot columns from RREF.
\(\text{Row}(A)\) = Span of rows of \(A\). Basis: nonzero rows of RREF of \(A\). Row operations preserve row space, not column space.
\(\{\mathbf{v}_1,\ldots,\mathbf{v}_k\}\) is LI iff \(c_1\mathbf{v}_1 + \cdots + c_k\mathbf{v}_k = \mathbf{0} \implies c_1 = \cdots = c_k = 0\).
Set \(\sum c_i p_i(t) = 0\) (zero polynomial). Match coefficients of \(1, t, t^2, \ldots\) independently. Solve system. LI iff all \(c_i = 0\).
S is a basis for V iff (1) S is LI and (2) S spans V. Both conditions required.

\(\text{rank}(A) + \text{nullity}(A) = n\) where \(n\) = number of columns. \(\text{rank}(A) = \dim\text{Col}(A) = \dim\text{Row}(A) = \#\text{pivots}\). \(\text{nullity}(A) = \dim\text{Null}(A) = \#\text{free variables}\).

If \(\mathcal{B}=\{\mathbf{b}_1,\ldots,\mathbf{b}_n\}\) is a basis: \([\mathbf{x}]_\mathcal{B} = (c_1,\ldots,c_n)^T\) where \(\mathbf{x} = c_1\mathbf{b}_1+\cdots+c_n\mathbf{b}_n\). Find by row-reducing \([\mathbf{b}_1 \mid \cdots \mid \mathbf{b}_n \mid \mathbf{x}]\).

Front: Matrix of T relative to basis \(\mathcal{B}\) (Lay 4.7)
Back: \(M_\mathcal{B} = \bigl[[T(\mathbf{b}_1)]_\mathcal{B} \mid \cdots \mid [T(\mathbf{b}_n)]_\mathcal{B}\bigr]\). Columns = \(\mathcal{B}\)-coordinate vectors of images of basis vectors. Apply \(T\) to each basis vector; express result in \(\mathcal{B}\)-coordinates.

\(\lambda\) is an eigenvalue of \(A\) iff \(\exists\) nonzero \(\mathbf{v}\) with \(A\mathbf{v} = \lambda\mathbf{v}\). Equivalently: \(\lambda\) is eigenvalue \(\iff \det(A - \lambda I) = 0 \iff (A - \lambda I)\) is singular.
\(E_\lambda = \text{Null}(A - \lambda I)\). Basis: row-reduce \((A - \lambda I)\), write parametric solution, extract free-variable vectors. \(E_\lambda\) is always a subspace.
\(p(\lambda) = \det(A - \lambda I)\). Eigenvalues = roots of \(p(\lambda) = 0\). Degree \(= n\) for \(n \times n\) matrix.
Eigenvalues = diagonal entries. Valid ONLY IF \(A\) is upper or lower triangular.

Alg. mult\((\lambda_0)\) = power of \((\lambda - \lambda_0)\) in \(p(\lambda)\). Geo. mult\((\lambda_0)\) = \(\dim \text{Null}(A - \lambda_0 I)\). Always: \(1 \leq \text{geo. mult} \leq \text{alg. mult}\).
\(A\) diagonalizable \(\iff\) geo. mult\((\lambda)\) = alg. mult\((\lambda)\) for ALL eigenvalues \(\lambda\). Equivalently: \(\mathbb{R}^n\) has a basis of eigenvectors of \(A\).
\(n\) distinct eigenvalues \(\implies A\) diagonalizable. Sufficient only — converse FAILS: repeated eigenvalues do not imply non-diagonalizable.
\(A^k = PD^kP^{-1}\), \(D^k = \text{diag}(\lambda_1^k,\ldots,\lambda_n^k)\). PRECONDITION (iff): \(A\) must be diagonalizable. If not diagonalizable, formula does not apply.
If \(A\) real and \(\lambda = a+bi\) is eigenvalue \(\implies \bar{\lambda} = a-bi\) also eigenvalue. Eigenvectors conjugate pairs. Requires \(A\) real.

\(\mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v} = \sum u_i v_i\). Properties: symmetric \((\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}=\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{u})\); linear in each argument; \(\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{u} \geq 0\); \(\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{u}=0 \iff \mathbf{u}=\mathbf{0}\).

\(\mathbf{u} \perp \mathbf{v} \iff \mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v} = 0\). Pythagorean identity (iff): \(\|\mathbf{u}+\mathbf{v}\|^2 = \|\mathbf{u}\|^2 + \|\mathbf{v}\|^2 \iff \mathbf{u} \perp \mathbf{v}\).
An orthogonal set (no zero vectors) is LI. Proof: dot \(\sum c_i \mathbf{u}_i = \mathbf{0}\) with each \(\mathbf{u}_j\); orthogonality forces \(c_j = 0\).
\(U\) has orthonormal columns \(\iff U^T U = I\). Does NOT imply \(UU^T = I\) unless \(U\) is square.

\(\text{proj}_{\mathbf{u}}\,\mathbf{y} = \dfrac{\mathbf{y}\cdot\mathbf{u}}{\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{u}}\,\mathbf{u}\). PRECONDITION: \(\mathbf{u} \neq \mathbf{0}\) (\(\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{u} = 0 \iff \mathbf{u}=\mathbf{0}\), denominator undefined).

\(\hat{\mathbf{y}} = \sum_i \frac{\mathbf{y}\cdot\mathbf{u}_i}{\mathbf{u}_i\cdot\mathbf{u}_i}\mathbf{u}_i\) where \(\{\mathbf{u}_1,\ldots,\mathbf{u}_k\}\) orthogonal basis for \(W\). PRECONDITION: basis must be orthogonal. If not, run Gram-Schmidt first.

\(\mathbf{y} = \hat{\mathbf{y}} + \mathbf{z}\) where \(\hat{\mathbf{y}} \in W\) and \(\mathbf{z} = \mathbf{y} - \hat{\mathbf{y}} \perp W\). Verify: \(\mathbf{z}\cdot\mathbf{u}_i = 0\) for each basis vector. Distance to \(W\) = \(\|\mathbf{z}\|\).

Input: LI \(\{\mathbf{x}_1,\ldots,\mathbf{x}_p\}\). \(\mathbf{u}_1 = \mathbf{x}_1\); \(\mathbf{u}_k = \mathbf{x}_k - \sum_{j<k} \frac{\mathbf{x}_k\cdot\mathbf{u}_j}{\mathbf{u}_j\cdot\mathbf{u}_j}\mathbf{u}_j\). Span preserved at each step. Normalize: \(\mathbf{e}_i = \mathbf{u}_i/\|\mathbf{u}_i\|\).
\(A^T A\,\hat{\mathbf{x}} = A^T\mathbf{b}\). Always valid — no invertibility precondition on this equation.

\(\hat{\mathbf{x}} = (A^T A)^{-1} A^T \mathbf{b}\). PRECONDITION (iff): \(A^T A\) invertible \(\iff\) columns of \(A\) are LI \(\iff\) \(A\) has full column rank. If \(A\) rank-deficient: \(A^T A\) singular, formula undefined. Use QR or pseudoinverse \(A^+\).

\(\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}^{-1} = \frac{1}{ad-bc}\begin{pmatrix}d&-b\\-c&a\end{pmatrix}\). PRECONDITION (iff): \(ad - bc \neq 0\). If \(ad-bc=0\): singular matrix, division by zero — undefined.
\(\|\mathbf{b} - A\hat{\mathbf{x}}\|\) = norm of residual. Geometrically: distance from \(\mathbf{b}\) to \(\text{Col}(A)\). Zero \(\iff \mathbf{b} \in \text{Col}(A)\) (system was consistent).
